messages.author: 17d9c7a6e1a581b8
messages.subject: meeting / next point release
parts:
Hi,

I can't make the meeting today either.

The only thing I'd like to have talked about is a rough time frame for 2.2.1. If
everything goes smoothly it takes a couple of hours for me to update PyStan --
but being able to know when I will need to set time aside for that is helpful.

The other case for (somewhat) more frequent minor point releases is that it
might help surface minor bugs with new or changed code. This seems especially
useful with all the API refactoring.

Thanks,

-a

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] meeting / next point release
parts:
I think we're just waiting for tests to trickle
through Jenkins at this point before releasing 2.3.0. My
to-do list is empty, so if anyone thinks I should be doing
someting else for 2.3.0, let me know. I'm hammered for
the next three weeks or so (grant proposal due, Betancourt
and others visiting, then a one week trip).

I'm afraid there's no real timeline. We could try to get
better at that, but it's going to be tricky given the nature
of bugs cropping up and the mostly part-time commitment to
the project.

More frequent releases are a delicate balance. Users don't
like too-frequent updates or too-infrequent ones (or so they
tell us), but I'm not sure whether (a) to trust them, or (b) what
the right release schedule is.

It's definitely worth talking about at a meeting when you and
Daniel can make it.

- Bob
